memory_update.text: MOD should remain in the data_center_thermal_storage_controls universe as a high-evidence thermal-capacity supplier because of the May 26, 2026 $4B Airedale data-center cooling capacity agreement and explicit liquid-cooling/intelligent-controls product language.

INV should be tracked only as a speculative_shadow candidate: Accelsius has direct two-phase liquid-cooling relevance and strategic-investor validation, but evidence must move from announcements to audited revenue, deployments, and ownership economics.

The thermal bottleneck is not only chillers; the strongest node relation appears to be integrated site-level cooling capacity, including liquid cooling, heat rejection, intelligent controls, deployment services, and customer-funded manufacturing capacity.

Next Layer 1B pass should separately scan UPS batteries, battery enclosures, fire suppression, inverter/EMS software, pumps, heat exchangers, dielectric fluids, and commissioning/testing providers so the universe is not overly weighted toward cooling OEMs.

node: Liquid cooling, heat rejection, battery storage, power controls, inverters, fire safety, and energy management software
summary: Layer 1B expansion for the site-level data-center thermal/power reliability stack. The broad bottleneck hypothesis remains plausible: AI data-center density is forcing power, cooling, controls, and reliability equipment to be specified as an integrated system rather than as standalone HVAC or electrical parts. This pass keeps Vertiv as the obvious reference leader, but the discovery lane points to Modine as a more focused thermal-capacity supplier with unusually strong order evidence, and Innventure/Accelsius as a small-cap speculative shadow candidate tied to two-phase direct-to-chip liquid cooling. No buy/sell view is provided.
